$comment: Server lane (lossless analytics) recipe vectors, shared with the receiving side. Every hex value is lowercase HMAC-SHA256 under `secret`. visitKey message = "visit:" + clientIp + "|" + userAgent + "|" + floor(epochSeconds / 1800); documentEventId = "doc:" + HMAC(visitKey + "|" + path + "|" + occurredAtMs); the body signature is HMAC over the exact JSON bytes of `documentEventBody`; the receipt request (GET …/server-lane/receipt?since=<iso>) signature is HMAC over the RAW QUERY STRING as sent (`receiptQuery`). The OUTCOME vectors cover the optional `adMatch` block (the Meta Conversions API relay): `outcomeEmail` hashed with sha256 of the TRIMMED, LOWERCASED address gives `outcomeEmailHash`, and the signature is HMAC over the exact JSON bytes of `outcomeAdMatchBody` — key order included, since the signature is over bytes, not over a parsed object. The block also carries the BUYER'S BROWSER `client_ip_address` and `client_user_agent`, copied by the customer's server from ITS OWN inbound request — never from the (server-to-server) call to Infinite, whose ip and user agent describe the customer's host. adMatch is consumed by the relay at ingest and never stored.

outcomeResponses.$comment: The 202 the server-events route answers (build plan section 3j.1), and what reportInfiniteOutcome resolves for each. metaEventId is non-null ONLY for an accepted, first-time outcome the relay will send AND a named Meta event; a duplicate, a relay that is off, or an unreadable reply resolves null, so the browser never mirrors.

cases.name: an id without a name is not an instruction

outcomeWireIds.$comment: reportInfiniteOutcome sends the wire eventId "<type>:<eventId>" (build plan section 3z.10, B16); once that passes 160 characters it sends "<type>:" + the sha256 hex of the eventId. One stable id reused for two outcome types never collides. The echoed metaEventId is the wire id.
